studies.label: Between-subjects brainstorming experiment: human-only vs human + GLM (food waste)

counts_source.quote: Of the remaining 75 participants (age: mean = 23.3, min = 18, max = 37 years; gender: 13 female, 62 male), all but one are in study programs at the informatics department.

arms.name: human + GLM
arms.description: Individual brainstorming in the purpose-built app with its GLM function active. Participants request suggestions using a fixed-prompt Generate ideas button and may copy, edit, or ignore them; at least one request was required (PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 1031-1032, Sects. 3.2-3.3).

arms.name: human-only
arms.description: Individual brainstorming in the same app with its GLM function deactivated (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1031, Sect. 3.2).

studies.task: Brainstorm for 10 minutes on “How can we reduce food waste?”, then select the four best ideas from the long list (PDF p. 8, printed p. 1030, Sect. 3.1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 1033, Sect. 3.5).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 (temperature 0.9), embedded in the brainstorming app
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 1031), Sect. 3.3; model and temperature explicitly named, model release year not stated

studies.shared_sample: The screening form flags possible overlap with Memmert and Bittner (2024; c861), based on matching participant quotations and c861's statement that it reanalyzes a previous study, and flags related ECIS reports. The present paper cites these reports without declaring shared participants. The identity and number of overlapping quantitative participants remain unconfirmed; do not assume independent samples. Source: forms/c098.json, sample_overlap; the matching quotation in this paper is on PDF p. 15 (printed p. 1037), Sect. 4.4.1.

estimates.notes: This robustness outcome counts qualifying ideas, so it is coded as fluency/category_count; its form_outcome_id links to the screening form's novelty or value outcome under which the robustness analysis is described. The threshold is a pooled rating cutoff, not an arm mean. Threshold quotation (PDF p. 13, printed p. 1035, Sect. 4.1): “above average ideas for novelty (mean = 3.396) and value (mean = 4.747), respectively, in the long-lists of ideas.” n_total uses the printed common analytic sample in Sect. 3.4. Good-Idea-Count uses the long list independently of shortlist selection (PDF p. 11, printed p. 1033, Sect. 3.5), and no further long-list exclusions are reported. open_items: The number randomized and labeled per-arm analyzed counts are not printed. Sect. 3.4 (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1032) reports 77 completers and two exclusions, with 75 remaining participants. Sect. 3.6 (PDF p. 12, printed p. 1034) gives unlabeled group sizes of 38 and 37; these cannot be assigned to named arms. For human-level shortlist quality, four treated participants were excluded, but the resulting analysis total is not printed; the GPT-4 shortlist analyses also have no explicit final count. Those estimate counts remain null. Long-list Good-Idea-Count records use the printed common analytic sample, because the outcome is explicitly independent of shortlist selection and no additional long-list exclusions are stated; robustness-specific counts are not repeated beside the tests.

Participant-level arm SDs, SEs, and numerical confidence limits are absent. Only human-judge dyad novelty has printed arm means. The interval type and endpoints in Fig. 8c (PDF p. 13, printed p. 1035) are not stated; no statistics were digitized or derived.
Human-fluency significance conflicts: Sect. 4.1 prints p = 0.015, while Fig. 7a uses ** with caption **p < .01 (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 1034-1035). The text value is retained.

For human fluency the paper prints a negative rank-biserial correlation but a positive converted Cohen’s d; no conversion formula or SD denominator is specified. The standardizer for the human-judge dyad novelty Cohen’s d is also not defined (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 1034-1035).

The Good-Idea-Count novelty threshold is printed as 3.396 in Sect. 4.1 and the same number is printed as the treated dyad-level human-judge novelty mean in Sect. 4.2 (PDF p. 13, printed p. 1035). All numerical stats and counts were checked against the PDF source quotations; no effects, SDs, SEs, confidence limits, or participant counts were derived. Printed medians are retained in notes and their source quotations without adding fields outside the prescribed stats structure. The second human-fluency effect, the paper's positive converted Cohen's d, is also preserved in notes; the signed rank-biserial correlation is the structured effect. All source quotations are at most forty words and normalize PDF line wrapping, line-end hyphenation, ligatures, and font-extraction substitutes for plus and less-than signs. Fig. 7a was inspected in memory to confirm its significance-label conflict. No figure coordinates were used to extract numbers. Human and dyad outcomes, and their robustness variants, share participants and the control arm. Preregistered status and primary-outcome status remain not_stated.
